review_notes: I reviewed the whole file: two theorems with no simp attributes, and one simp-call proof. I also read StrictMono.sign_comp in Mathlib's Sign/Defs.lean and scaleRoots_eval₂_mul in ScaleRoots.lean. I checked the downstream uses. Thom/Basic.lean:256 and OneSided.lean:137 apply sign_eval_map with `exact`. Semialgebraic/Thom.lean:79 uses sign_eval₂_C_pow_mul_scaleRoots in `rw`. Nothing in these uses needs a simp lemma. Both statements have a hypothesis-bearing, non-canonical shape. Their left-hand sides, such as `sign ((p.map f).eval (f x))`, are not stable simp normal forms, because Mathlib's eval_map-style lemmas would rewrite them first. Tagging either with simp would add competing rules and so is not justified. The proof's simp call lists explicit lemmas, which is fine. I found no cycle, competing rule, bad orientation or missing canonical simp lemma. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out subtle simp behavior.
